Elephanta
------------------------------------------
It is an island situated about 11 kilometres (7 miles) from the Bombay (now Mumbai) harbour to the north-east. Its circumference is about 7 kilometers (4½ miles). Its original name was Śrīpurī or Ghārāpurī and was attached to the Konkan region of Maharashtra. It was under the political control of several dynasties of kings like Western Cāḷukyas, Cāḷukyas under Pulakeśin II (A.
), the Yādavas of Devagiri and so on, before coming under British rule in A.

.
शिव at एलेफन्त Caves">Trimūrti शिव at एलेफन्त CavesThe island got its name due to the images of elephants—now missing—on the steps of one of the temples there. It is famous for its archaeological monuments, especially the six चवे तेम्प्लेस् belonging to the Śaiva cults, assigned to the 8th century A. D.
The largest of these caves in solid rock faces north. It is 39 metres (130 ft.) long. The width is also, approximately, the same. But there are mukhamaṇṭapas—subsidiary halls—measuring 16 metres (54 ft.) by 5 metres (16½ ft.) in the west, the north and the east. The average height is 5 metres (16 to 17 ft.). There is a small sanctum with a लिङ्ग, towards the west. It also has two figures of the dvārapālakas (gate-keepers).
The एलेफन्त caves contain a number of huge images (of the relief type) of the Śaiva cult. They are 3.6 to 5.4 metres (12 to 18 ft.) in height. The most important of these images is that of महेश्वर शिव, also called ‘Trimūrti-शिव’. The main face represents the Tatpuruṣa or महादेव aspect of शिव. This face is serene and beautiful. It has a जटामुकुट (hair dressed up as a crown). The other two faces are those of अघोर or भैरव and वामदेव or Umā. The depiction of several—often contradictory—moods in the same image shows the excellence of workmanship. The whole image, sculptured from the chest upwards, is inside a depression in the back wall, 3 metres (10 ft.) in depth and 6 metres (21 ft.) in width.
There are eight more images, all of शिव in his various aspects. Some of them are: नटराज, शिव in meditation, रावण shaking the कैलास mountain, शिव killing Andhakāsura and Ardhanārīśvara.
